show: Professor Brian Cox Live Q and A Podcast
einzeiler: Professor Brian Cox answers audience questions on physics, black holes, and the cosmos.
kurzfassung: Professor Brian Cox answers a variety of audience-submitted questions ranging from theoretical physics and black holes to the search for extraterrestrial life. During the live Q&A session, he explains complex cosmological concepts like quantum mechanics, dark matter, and the expansion of the universe in an accessible way. Co-host Robin Ince adds humor and banter throughout the discussions on science and history.
stichpunkte: Quarks are currently the smallest known building blocks of protons and neutrons.
Supermassive black holes will take approximately 10 to the power of 100 years to evaporate.
The Rosetta spacecraft mission ended with a controlled crash onto a comet to study pristine solar system material.
The many worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics posits that every probability is realized in an infinite number of universes.
Dark matter and dark energy make up roughly 95 percent of the universe, with the remaining 5 percent being normal matter.
The Fermi paradox questions why we have not detected alien civilizations despite the vast number of Earth-like planets.
Water is considered the ideal solvent for carbon chemistry and the spontaneous generation of life.
Charles Darwin and Albert Einstein are highlighted as inspirational historical scientists.

kapitel.titel: The Rosetta Spacecraft and Quantum Mechanics
The Moon, Solar Flares, and Transistors
The Universe, Dark Energy, and Dark Matter
Extraterrestrial Life and the Fermi Paradox

clips.hook: How long until black holes evaporate?
clips.text: The largest supermassive black holes require an unimaginably long duration measured with a one followed by one hundred zeros to fully return their energy.

clips.hook: Why are our days getting longer?
clips.text: The moon drifts further away from Earth on an annual basis, which alters rotational momentum and gradually extends the length of a day.

clips.hook: What is the universe actually made of?
clips.text: Visible stars and galaxies account for only a tiny fraction of the cosmos, while the vast majority consists of mysterious dark matter and energy.

clips.hook: How many Earth-like planets are out there?
clips.text: Telescope observations suggest that the Milky Way alone harbors tens of billions of planets with conditions similar to Earth.

clips.hook: The absurd reality of early science journalism
clips.text: After discovering pulsars, a pioneering female astronomer received no mainstream press attention except for one tabloid inquiring about her height.

beschreibung: In the first episode of this brand new series, we present a selection of the questions posed to Professor Brian Cox from the audience, via Robin Ince, from the first two weeks of the tour. There's queries about quarks, the age of the universe and plenty more. This podcast was recorded live from the shows in Manchester and Newcastle.
